issues.claim: A flag baked in at build time is a special and the least convenient case ... it is exactly the kind that does not separate deployment from release.
issues.problem: This contradicts the cited Fowler/Hodgson excerpt. It says a Release Toggle decision is "typically very static" and that changing it by rolling out a new release with a toggle configuration change is "usually perfectly acceptable". Release toggles are described as "the most common way" to separate release from deployment. A static or config-baked flag still decouples merging and deploying unfinished code from exposing it to users. Saying it "does not separate deployment from release" teaches the wrong lesson.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep c wrong because of the absolute "every flag value needs its own build". Rewrite the explanation along these lines. The flag value is usually read at run time from configuration or a flag service, so no new build is needed. Release toggles are often fairly static, and a config-only change or redeploy is sometimes acceptable. Even then the unfinished code is already integrated and deployed, so this is not required for every flag. Drop the claim that a build-time flag "does not separate deployment from release". Apply the same change in ru.

issues.claim: Сам флаг и старая ветка кода - временный долг
issues.problem: "Ветка кода" can be read as a git branch, but the intended meaning is the old code path (the if/else branch). The en text says "code path".
issues.suggestedFix: Replace with "старый путь выполнения (ветвь кода)" or "старая ветвь `if`".

issues.claim: Option a is much longer and more detailed than b, c and d
issues.problem: The correct answer is recognisable by length alone.
issues.suggestedFix: Shorten option a, or lengthen the distractors to a comparable size.

issues.claim: Every flag adds a branch to the code and doubles the number of paths to test.
issues.problem: The article excerpt does not show this "doubling" claim, and it is an oversimplification. The paths multiply only for combinations of flags that can be on at the same time.
issues.suggestedFix: Say "adds a branch and multiplies the paths that must be tested".

issues.claim: the cache keeps the package set of the first run forever
issues.problem: GitHub evicts cache entries not accessed for 7 days, and there are size limits. "Forever" overstates this, though the point that an exact-hit key is not overwritten is correct for actions/cache.
issues.suggestedFix: Write "keeps serving the package set saved by the first run for as long as the entry exists". Make the same change in ru.

issues.claim: there is never an exact key match
issues.problem: Re-running a job on the same commit does hit the same SHA key, so "never" is slightly too strong.
issues.suggestedFix: Write "a new commit never gets an exact key match". Make the same change in ru.
